jobs.description: Emergency Medicine Physician - Clinical Assistant/Associate/Full Professor Apply now Job no: 540982 Work type: Non-Tenure-Track Faculty Location: Jacksonville Campus Categories: Education/Training/Instructional Design, Medicine/Physicians Department:30290000 - JX-EMERGENCY MEDICINE-JAX Classification Title: CLIN AST/ASO/FULL PROF Classification Minimum Requirements: Must be MD/DO and get a medical license in the State of Florida. Job Description: The University of Florida Department of Emergency Medicine - Jacksonville is recruiting a motivated and energetic board certified or board-eligible emergency medicine physician to join our department in a Community Faculty position. This will be a non-tenured position up to a 1.00 FTE. Clinical activity occurs at a variety of sites and works alongside colleagues in other specialty services. Successful candidates will receive an appointment as either a Clinical Assistant, Clinical Associate or Clinical Professor. Qualified candidates must be ABEM/ABOEM board eligible or certified. About UF Health: UF Health is Southeast’s premier academic health center and an integral part of the University of Florida. Our mission is to promote health through outstanding and high-quality patient care, innovative and rigorous education in the health professions and biomedical sciences, and research across the spectrum of basic, translational and clinical investigation. UF Health encompasses the Gainesville-based University of Florida colleges of Dentistry, Medicine, Nursing, Pharmacy, Public Health and Health Professions, and Veterinary Medicine; the UF Health Shands family of hospitals in Gainesville; UF Health Jacksonville medical center; UF Health North; an academic campus in Jacksonville that is home to the UF College of Medicine – Jacksonville and includes degree programs offered by the colleges of Nursing and Pharmacy; UF Health St. Johns in St. Augustine; UF Health Neighborhood Hospital in Ocala; and our campus in Central Florida, which includes UF Health Spanish Plaines Hospital and UF Health Leesburg Hospital. It also includes primary care and specialty practices throughout Central, North Central and northern Florida and Southeast Georgia. The UF Health network of hospitals and physician practices manages more than 3 million inpatient and outpatient visits each year, and serves patients from all 67 Florida counties, from across the nation and from dozens of countries around the world. About College of Medicine – Jacksonville (COM-J): The UF College of Medicine – Jacksonville is the largest of the three colleges at the Health Science Center Jacksonville. The college's 16 clinical science departments house more than 500 faculty members, 1,560 staff and 450 residents and fellows, as well as medical students from UF and around the country. We offer an incredible breadth of clinical training programs and proud to train many of best primary care providers and specialists throughout the region, the state and the country. Research, discovery and innovation are critical aspects of our clinical campus and we have some of the country’s leading researchers at our locations searching for and finding new treatments and clinical options. The UF College of Medicine – Jacksonville faculty, administrators, residents, fellows, students and staff work as a team in pursuit of our common mission — to heal, to comfort, to educate and to discover through quality health care, elimination of health disparities, medical education, innovation and research. To learn more about our college, leadership, mission, faculty resources, and the city of Jacksonville visit https://med.jax.ufl.edu/administrative-affairs/faculty-orientation-guide/. Expected Salary: Salary and academic appointment is negotiable and the benefits are excellent. Required Qualifications: Must be MD/DO and get a medical license in the State of Florida. jobs.description: Department English Language Program-OPS Compensation $30.00 Hourly Job Responsibilities The English Language Program accepts applications on an ongoing basis to maintain a pool of qualified ESL instructors. Instructors are hired as teaching needs arise based on student enrollment, program needs, and instructor availability. Applicants may be contacted when teaching opportunities become available. Employment is offered on a semester-by-semester basis. Job Functions An ESL Instructor provides English language instruction to multilingual and international students at the University of North Florida’s English Language Program. Students come from a variety of countries and linguistic backgrounds and study English for a range of goals, including preparing for university admission and advancing their professional lives. The English Language Program offers six proficiency levels: Beginning 00, High-Beginning 10, Intermediate 20, High-Intermediate 30, Advanced 40, and Pre-University 50. Courses focus primarily on general and academic English, with instruction in reading/writing, listening/speaking/vocabulary, and grammar. The ESL Instructor position is a part-time, in-person position in our Day Program. The Day Program operates Monday–Thursday, 9:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m., for three semesters per year: spring, summer, and fall. A full teaching schedule is 3 classes per day, approximately 26 hours per week. Reduced schedules of 1–2 classes per day may also be available. Instructors indicate their availability when scheduling, and semester assignments are made based on instructor availability, enrollment, and program needs. ESL Instructors are assigned specific courses each semester but should be prepared to teach across subject areas and proficiency levels as program needs require. Required Qualifications •Bachelor's degree in English, TESOL, Applied Linguistics, Second Language Acquisition, English Education, or a related field. •Experience teaching English to multilingual learners from diverse linguistic and cultural backgrounds. •Knowledge and experience teaching academic English. •Ability to manage a classroom effectively and create an engaging learning environment. ESL Instructors: Prepare and deliver engaging English language lessons using established curriculum materials along with instructor-developed supplemental materials. Teach assigned courses in reading/writing, listening/speaking/vocabulary, and grammar across the program's six proficiency levels. Assess student learning and provide appropriate feedback/academic support to students. Maintain effective classroom management and create a positive, engaging learning environment. Attend faculty meetings and collaborate with instructors within the program. Proctor final examinations. Hold one paid office hour per week. Reading/Writing instructors hold one additional paid tutoring hour per week. Preparation, grading, and other instructional responsibilities are included within the scheduled teaching hours. Preferred Qualifications: Master's degree in TESOL, Applied Linguistics, Second Language Acquisition, or a related field. Experience teaching ESL/EFL in higher education or university-preparation programs. Experience teaching English abroad. Statement(s) of Understanding This position requires a background check. Overview: The University of Miami, UHealth is pleased to offer a one-year non-ACGME fellowship in Cardiovascular Advanced Imaging. This specialized training program is designed for physicians who are looking to deepen their expertise in cardiovascular imaging techniques, with a particular focus on advanced imaging modalities used for the diagnosis and management of cardiovascular diseases. The program provides comprehensive hands-on training in state-of-the-art imaging technologies, including but not limited to cardiac MRI, cardiac CT, and echocardiography. Objectives: The Cardiovascular Advanced Imaging Fellowship at UHealth aims to provide advanced training in the clinical and technical aspects of cardiovascular imaging. Fellows will gain experience in interpreting and performing imaging studies to enhance diagnostic and therapeutic decision-making for complex cardiovascular patients. Responsibilities: Clinical Training : Participate in daily clinical practice with a multidisciplinary team, interpreting advanced cardiovascular imaging modalities including cardiac CT, MRI, echocardiography, and nuclear imaging. Advanced Imaging Techniques : Obtain expertise in advanced techniques such as myocardial perfusion imaging, coronary artery imaging, cardiac function evaluation, and tissue characterization using state-of-the-art imaging modalities. Research Opportunities : Engage in clinical and translational research projects related to cardiovascular imaging. Fellows will have the opportunity to collaborate with faculty on ongoing studies and contribute to publications in high-impact journals. Collaboration with Specialists : Work closely with cardiologists, radiologists, and other specialists to develop integrated treatment strategies for patients with complex cardiovascular conditions. Educational Activities : Participate in didactic teaching sessions, case discussions, and regular departmental conferences. Fellows will also be encouraged to present at local and national meetings. Quality Assurance and Protocol Development : Gain experience in quality assurance processes and protocol development to ensure accurate imaging results and effective clinical utilization. Qualifications: Education : MD or equivalent degree. Completion of an ACGME-accredited residency in Internal Medicine, Cardiology, Radiology, or other relevant specialty. Experience : Previous experience in cardiovascular imaging is highly preferred, though motivated applicants with strong backgrounds in cardiology or radiology will be considered. Licensure : Must be eligible for licensure in the state of Florida. Skills : Strong analytical, communication, and organizational skills. Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, multidisciplinary environment. Research Interest : Interest in cardiovascular imaging research and its clinical applications. Academic Development : Opportunities to engage in high-quality research and contribute to academic publications. Professional Networking : Exposure to a diverse clinical and research network, with opportunities to collaborate with leading experts in the field of cardiovascular imaging. To learn how to apply for a faculty or staff position, please review this tip sheet . Miami is rapidly emerging as a leading global hub for innovation and technology. As the seventh-largest metro area in the United States and one of the fastest-growing cities, Miami continues to attract top talent and investment, particularly in the fields of Technology, FinTech, Artificial Intelligence, and Healthcare. With its unique combination of cultural diversity, entrepreneurial spirit, no state income taxes, and favorable climate, Miami is drawing a massive influx of wealth and expertise from around the world. The city is positioning itself as a center for cutting-edge developments in financial technology, healthcare analytics, life sciences, green technology, and digital transformation. We are one of the largest private employers in Miami, home to more than 16,000 faculty and staff from across the globe. The Miami Herbert Business School (MHBS) at the University of Miami plans to appoint four tenured or tenure-track faculty members in business and management, with a specific focus on attracting top talent in strategic areas of differentiation, such as Finance, Artificial Intelligence, Business Analytics, Healthcare, Innovation, Entrepreneurship, and Sustainability. Boundary spanning scholars who can work in multiple strategic areas are preferred. These positions will: Support growth and provide scholarly and pedagogical expertise related to financial engineering, digital marketing, business analytics, data science, workforce management, artificial intelligence, healthcare analytics, sustainable business, innovation and entrepreneurship and other related fields. Bring visibility, reputation, and additional impact to our departments and programs. Help us achieve our goal of engaging with Miami’s rapidly growing finance, technology, entrepreneurship, and innovation community. These appointments will help build the University of Miami and the Miami Herbert Business School (MHBS) into internationally recognized incubators for new, high-impact, interdisciplinary ideas at the cutting edge of business and technology. The University of Miami is among the top-tier higher education institutions in the U.S., known for its academic excellence, superior medical care, and cutting-edge research. At the U, we are committed to attracting a talented workforce to support our mission of transforming lives through education, research, innovation, and service. Through our values of Diversity, Integrity, Responsibility, Excellence, Compassion, Creativity, and Teamwork, we strive to create an environment where everyone contributes to making the U a great place to work. Job Description: The Department of Surgery at the University of Florida College of Medicine – Jacksonville, is seeking an Otorhinolaryngologist at the non-tenure accruing level of Clinical Assistant, Associate, or Professor in the Division of Otorhinolaryngology – Head and Neck Surgery. The Department of Surgery at the University of Florida College of Medicine – Jacksonville is a tertiary referral center that serves the population of Northeast Florida and Southeast Georgia. It is home to the divisions of General Surgery/Surgical Oncology, Otorhinolaryngology, Plastic Surgery, and Trauma/Acute Care/Critical Care. We are transforming the Division of Otorhinolaryngology – Head and Neck Surgery to serve our growing community through multidisciplinary care and collaboration. Our focus is on building subspecialty centers of clinical excellence to meet our vision of being the regions most valued surgical health care asset. The division currently offers thriving practices in Laryngology, Otology, Rhinology, with continued growth in Head and Neck Surgery and Facial Plastics/Reconstruction. Additionally, the division will provide comprehensive general otorhinolaryngology services and currently serves as a key leader of the UF Health Skull Base Center. The Chief will lead the growth of the elective surgical practice throughout the Northeast Florida and Southeast Georgia region with a focus on high-quality academic medical care. The division is poised for growth and we are excited to offer this opportunity. The duties and responsibilities of the position include, but are not limited to: Provide and maintain a high level of quality outpatient intermediate care services in all aspects of Otorhinolaryngology Provide clinical teaching of trainees if applicable and participate in the educational program. Be responsible for excellent communication with primary care physicians and other consulting providers. Assist in marketing the Otorhinolaryngology programs to community physicians and managed care organizations. Participate in monthly division meetings, administrative functions and institutional committees as requested. About UF Health: UF Health is the Southeast’s premier academic health center and an integral part of the University of Florida. Our mission is to promote health through outstanding and high-quality patient care, innovative and rigorous education in the health professions and biomedical sciences, and research across the spectrum of basic, translational and clinical investigation. UF Health encompasses the Gainesville-based University of Florida colleges of Dentistry, Medicine, Nursing, Pharmacy, Public Health and Health Professions, and Veterinary Medicine; the UF Health Shands family of hospitals in Gainesville; UF Health Jacksonville medical center; UF Health North; an academic campus in Jacksonville that is home to the UF College of Medicine – Jacksonville and includes degree programs offered by the colleges of Nursing and Pharmacy; UF Health St. Johns in St. Augustine; UF Health Neighborhood Hospital in Ocala; and our campus in Central Florida, which includes UF Health Spanish Plaines Hospital and UF Health Leesburg Hospital. Faculty members are jointly appointed to create synergies and collective strength, resulting in a competitive research profile and highly trained students who receive exceptional exposure to a variety of expertise. The department offers an epidemiology PhD, Master of Science, and concentration in the MPH program. It is also home to two National Institutes of Health Training grants (T32). Our research sits at the cutting edge of regenerative medicine and neurobiology, utilizing state-of-the-art human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) models, 3D tissue engineering, and advanced multi-omic / bioinformatics integrations to model and dissect human diseases. Our lab focuses heavily on inventing and reﬁning Next Approach Methodologies (NAMs)—speciﬁcally, brain organoids, Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB) / Blood-Spinal Cord Barrier (BSCB) assembloids, and spinal cord/motor neuron models—to investigate the molecular and epitranscriptomic mechanisms driving neurodegenerative conditions like Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) and Alzheimer’s Disease (AD), as well as neurodevelopmental conditions including autism and Fragile X Syndrome (FXS). The Guo Lab is exceptionally well-funded through major federal agencies and foundation awards—including NINDS, NIMH, NIDA, NIA, and the NSF—and regularly publishes in high-impact journals such as Nature, Cell Stem Cell, Nature Neuroscience, Nature Communications, Science Advances, Molecular Psychiatry, Advanced Science, The Journal of Clinical Investigation, Cell Discovery, and Protein & Cell. This position oﬀers an unparalleled opportunity to spearhead high-proﬁle projects, leverage robust resources, and work within the deeply collaborative, state-of-the-art academic ecosystem at UF Health and the McKnight Brain Institute. Key Responsibilities: • Advanced Cellular Engineering: Lead the directed diﬀerentiation of hiPSCs into highly enriched neural and vascular lineages (e.g., cortical neurons, motor neurons, astrocytes, microglia, brain endothelial cells, pericytes) to construct complex 3D assembloids and organ-on-a-chip platforms. • Mechanistic Dissection: Deploy CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing, shRNA/ASO tools, and pharmacological screens to interrogate pathological cellular axes. • Multimodal Analytics: Perform and integrate high-resolution functional readouts, including whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology, quantitative confocal/super-resolution microscopy, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and spatial transcriptomics. • Scientiﬁc Leadership: Independently manage project milestones, draft high-impact manuscripts, present ﬁndings at premier international conferences, and mentor graduate and undergraduate students within a supportive lab ecosystem. Expected Salary: $63,480-$65,000 commensurate with experience Required Qualifications: Ph.D. in Neurobiology, Stem Cell Biology, Biomedical Engineering, Cell Biology, Molecular Biology, or a closely related ﬁeld. Preferred: • Strong technical background in mammalian cell culture (experience with hiPSC/hESC maintenance and directed diﬀerentiation is highly preferred, but not required for candidates with exceptional molecular biology or electrophysiology expertise). • Hands-on experience with 3D organoid, assembloid, or microﬂuidic/organ-on-a-chip modeling. • Experience with whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology or multi-electrode arrays. • Familiarity with computational biology pipelines (e.g., handling transcriptomic or scRNA-seq datasets using R or Python). If an accommodation due to a disability is needed to apply for this position, please call 352-392-2477 or the Florida Relay System at 800-955-8771 (TDD) or visit Accessibility at UF . A postdoctoral research associate position is available in the laboratory of Dr. Zhonglin Mou in the Department of Microbiology and Cell Science at the University of Florida. The position is supported by a newly funded three-year USDA/NIFA grant focused on understanding extracellular immune signaling in plants. The successful candidate will investigate how extracellular signaling molecules, including extracellular NAD(P) and salicylic acid (SA), are sensed at the plant cell surface and how these signals activate local and systemic immune responses. Our research has identified lectin receptor kinases as key components of extracellular NAD(P) and SA signaling pathways that contribute to systemic acquired resistance (Li et al., Extracellular salicylic acid activates immune signaling through cell-surface receptors. bioRxiv 2026). The postdoctoral researcher will use molecular, genetic, biochemical, and cell biological approaches to define receptor activation mechanisms and determine how extracellular immune signaling interfaces with intracellular SA signaling and systemic immunity. Potential research areas include receptor-ligand interactions, receptor kinase activation and phosphorylation, protein-protein interactions, calcium and other early immune signaling events, genetic analysis of immune signaling pathways, and characterization of local and systemic disease resistance. The project provides opportunities to develop new mechanistic insights into plant immune signaling and to contribute to high-impact publications. The University of Florida is a Land-Grant, Sea-Grant, and Space-Grant institution, encompassing virtually all academic and professional disciplines, with an enrollment of more than 56,000 students. UF is a member of The Association of American Universities. The School of Natural Resources and Environment is an interdisciplinary unit housed in IFAS and managed by several colleges on campus. UF/IFAS employs nearly 4,500 people, which includes approximately 990 salaried faculty and 1,400 permanent support personnel located in Gainesville and throughout the state. IFAS, one of the nation’s largest agricultural and natural resources research and education organizations, is administered by a Vice President and four deans: the Dean of the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences, the Dean for Extension and Director of the Florida Cooperative Extension Service, the Dean for Research and Director of the Florida Agricultural Experiment Station, and the Dean for the College of Veterinary Medicine. jobs.description: Job Description The Opportunity Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University (ERAU), Daytona Beach Campus, invites applications for a full-time Postdoctoral Scholar position in the field of magnetospheric physics and space instrumentation. The successful candidate will contribute to cutting-edge research focused on the design and development of a miniature particle detector, as well as the analysis of satellite observations and numerical simulation results related to the Earth’s magnetosphere and space plasma environment. This position offers an exciting opportunity to work in a collaborative research environment at one of the world’s leading aerospace-focused universities. Position Responsibilities: Participate in the design, development, testing, and integration of a miniature particle detector for space applications. Analyze satellite measurements and numerical simulation results in the field of magnetospheric physics and space plasma science. Contribute to the development of data analysis tools and scientific interpretation of observational and modeling results. Prepare manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed journals and present research findings at scientific conferences. Assist with proposal development and contribute to externally funded research activities. Collaborate with faculty, students, and external research partners on interdisciplinary research initiatives. Mentoring and Career Development: This position includes a structured mentoring plan designed to support the professional growth of an early-career postdoctoral scientist and foster the development of independent research capabilities. Mentoring activities will include: Weekly one-on-one meetings focused on research progress, manuscript preparation, proposal development, and career planning. Regular group meetings to encourage collaboration, scientific communication, and presentation skills. Guidance in building a competitive research portfolio, securing external funding, leading research projects, and publishing high-impact research. Career development support will include: Periodic discussions to define long-term career goals and identify funding opportunities. Collaborative establishment of short- and medium-term milestones, including manuscript submissions and grant applications. Opportunities to take increasing ownership of research activities, including project leadership, collaboration management, and mentoring junior trainees. The overall goal of this mentoring framework is to support the successful transition of the postdoctoral scholar toward research independence and long-term career advancement. jobs.description: Professor and Miller Technology Endowed Chair in Financial Systems, The Barry S. Miller College of Business R114251 Main Campus, Orlando, Florida Faculty Full time Dean's Office - General - CBA View favorites The OpportunityThe Barry S. Miller College of Business at the University of Central Florida invites applications for the Miller Technology Endowed Chair in Financial Systems, a 9-month tenured position at the rank of professor. This position is located on the UCF Main Campus with an anticipated start date in Fall 2027. The central question addressed by this chair is: How should financial systems evolve to create, allocate, govern, and exchange capital in an increasingly intelligent, digital, and interconnected economy? Technologies such as artificial intelligence, digital platforms, blockchain, embedded finance, and advanced analytics are transforming financial institutions, markets, and organizational decision-making. We seek a scholar whose work advances understanding of financial systems, financial markets, financial institutions, accounting information systems, financial technology, corporate finance, banking, digital assets, financial regulation, or related areas. This endowed chair is part of a broader investment, five endowed chairs in all, each committed to advancing scholarship and education at the intersection of technology and business transformation. The Miller Chairs are not organized around traditional academic disciplines, but around consequential problems emerging from the intersection of technology, organizations, and markets. Miller Chairs are intended for scholars whose work has shaped—or has the clear potential to shape—how organizations function in a technology-driven economy. The successful candidate will play a central role in shaping the intellectual direction of the College’s technology-focused initiatives and will contribute to the School of Technology Leadership and Innovation (STLI), a university-wide initiative focused on translating advances in technology into organizational capability, market innovation, and executive practice. jobs.description: The School of Arts and Communication at Florida Institute of Technology seeks a Postdoctoral Research Associate as an active participant in the project “Cultivating Core Character through the General Education Core,” funded by Wake Forest University and the Lilly Endowment Inc. under co-PIs Lars Jones, Andrew Aberdein, and Heidi Hatfield Edwards. Beyond pursuing their own research agenda, the successful candidate will work under the supervision of project PIs and is expected to begin the 12-month annual position in January 2027 and continue through the end of the grant term in July 2029. Funds available for approved grant-related travel. Salary supplements may also be available. Specific responsibilities will include: · Teaching up to or the equivalent of two core undergraduate courses directly tied to our character education framework, ensuring pedagogical fidelity and integration with project goals. · Partnering with the PIs to support faculty and student virtue-education training, including workshops, mentoring, classroom sessions, and follow-up engagement. · Supporting the PIs in university-wide advocacy and outreach to other colleges as well as to the broader public. · Assisting the lead PI in designing and leading the biweekly character colloquium (topic selection, readings, integration with curriculum). · Attending weekly project team meetings. · Contributing to assessment planning, execution, and review to enable a rigorous evaluation of student and faculty outcomes. · Coordinating implementation and analysis of the project’s diagnostic framework, ensuring consistent data collection, interpretation, and integration across participating courses. · Collaborating on pedagogical scholarship tied to project activities and outputs, in addition to advancing their own research agenda. · Working with in-house support units, as well as student assistants, to help the PIs develop four Canvas LMS modules for scalable character education use in the University and beyond. Qualifications The successful candidate must have: · A PhD (either awarded or submitted and with defense formally scheduled) in a humanistic discipline, with a research specialization related to character education and/or virtue theory. · Demonstrated strong interest and ability in teaching. · Excellent communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills. · Ability to work both independently and as part of a team that must deal professionally with people at all levels. Schmidt College of Medicine at Florida Atlantic University seeks an accomplished surgeon-educator to serve as Surgery Clerkship Director, reporting to the Chair of the Department of Surgery with a secondary academic reporting relationship to the Associate Dean for Medical Education. This leadership role provides strategic direction and oversight for the required Surgery Clerkship within the College’s longitudinal integrated clinical curriculum, ensuring excellence in surgical education, student assessment, faculty engagement, and clinical learning experiences across affiliated training sites. The Surgery Clerkship Director will work closely with Undergraduate Medical Education leadership, faculty, residents, and affiliated clinical partners to advance curriculum innovation, continuous quality improvement, and compliance with LCME accreditation standards. This position includes a 0.5 FTE educational and administrative appointment and a 0.5 FTE clinical faculty appointment, with the expectation of maintaining an active surgical practice that supports outstanding patient care, bedside teaching, learner mentorship, and surgical resident education. Attend monthly Clerkship Director meetings and any additional meetings necessary to review student performance and curriculum implementation issues. Deliver surgery lectures to various levels of medical students each year and facilitate Diagnosis & Reasoning (DR) rounds for the clerkship students at the College of Medicine during in-person weekly academic half day. Develop, organize, and oversee the annual schedule of didactic lectures and educational activities, ensuring appropriate faculty participation and instructional quality. Prepare all student narrative comments for the surgery clerkship that will be included in the students’ Medical Student Performance Evaluation (MSPE/Dean’s Letter). jobs.description: Job Description The Opportunity The School of Graduate Studies in the College of Aviation at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University (ERAU) invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor/Associate Professor position with a strong preference for candidates with a background and expertise in air transportation systems, advanced air mobility, UAS traffic management, and machine learning/AI. Research Assistant Professor Positions (Research Track) The Department of Biomedical Engineering (BME) in the University of Miami (UM) College of Engineering, the Desai Sethi Urology Institute and the Miami Project to cure paralysis at UM Health system have multiple exciting opportunities for Research Assistant Professors , with the earliest start date of June 01, 2024. These positions are sponsored by multiple NIH Research Grants and UM to continue long-term research projects in the laboratory of Prof. Yingchun Zhang. Zhang's research aims to achieve the long-term goal of advancing Precision Rehabilitation. This will be accomplished through the comprehensive and quantitative assessment of dynamic activation and interactions of the brain, muscles, and brain-to-muscle pathways, using a combination of multimodal neuroimaging, neuroengineering, and neuromodulation techniques. Current research is dedicated to the advancement of innovative technologies aimed at achieving quantitative and precise diagnosis, phenotyping, and personalized treatment for a variety of neurological, neurodegenerative, and neuromuscular conditions. These conditions encompass psychiatric disorders, Alzheimer's disease (AD), stroke, spinal cord injury, pelvic floor dysfunctions, as well as the resultant movement disorders and pain conditions. The Research Assistant Professor will primarily work with Prof. Zhang and will also be embedded in the multidisciplinary team of investigators from BME at UM, and scientists/clinicians from the Desai Sethi Urology Institute and the Miami Project to cure paralysis at UM Health system. The position provides faculty level salary support, benefits, and a platform for professional growth including grant writing. Position Description and Requirements: Multimodal neuroimaging and neuroengineering: Developing novel technologies in precision diagnosis, phenotyping and personalized treatment of movement disorders, neuromuscular diseases and pain including the chronic pelvic pain. Experience in surface and intracranial EEG, ECoG, EMG, and/or tACS is desirable. Multimodal neuroimaging and neuromodulation: Developing novel techniques in precision diagnosis, phenotyping and personalized treatment of psychiatric disorders and Alzheimer's disease. Experience in surface and intracranial EEG, ECoG NIRS, MRI, TMS and/or Transcranial Focused Ultrasound is desirable. Regenerative rehabilitation: Developing regenerative therapies to enhance reduced muscle mass, restore impaired muscle innervation and co,ordination in conjunction with rehabilitative interventions. Experience in tissue engineering, extracorporeal shock wave therapy, and endogenous stem cell activation is desirable. Outstanding candidates with a MS or PhD degree in biomedical engineering, electrical engineering or relevant field, and strong publication records in relevant journals and outstanding writing and oral communication skills are encouraged to apply. Postdoctoral research experience is preferred. Interested applicants should send a curriculum vitae, statement describing research accomplishments and future research goals, relevant reprints, and the names of three references to y.zhang@miami.edu . jobs.description: Women's Imaging -Clinical Assistant/Associate Professor Apply now Job no: 541191 Work type: Non-Tenure-Track Faculty Location: Jacksonville Campus Categories: Education/Training/Instructional Design, Medicine/Physicians Department:30130000 - JX-RADIOLOGY-JACKSONVILLE Classification Title: CLIN AST ASO FULL PROF Classification Minimum Requirements: Candidate should have a MD/DO in Diagnostic Radiology Job Description: The University of Florida College of Medicine - Jacksonville (UF COM-J) Department of Radiology is seeking a fulltime Women's Imaging Radiologist at the non-tenure accruing level of Assistant/Associate/Full Professor Job responsibilities include: Women's Imaging Radiologist with academic focus at UF Jacksonville Health System at the Assistant, Associate Professor/Full Professor level with 100% specialization. Full-time academic position with UF Radiology and Imaging, UFJPI. Provide high quality service in a friendly academic setting. Serve as a mentor to train a great group of Residents & Fellows. Work with colleagues in surgery, oncology, radiation oncology & pathology, via daily interactions/multidisciplinary meetings. Have the drive and leadership skills necessary to be an integral part of the Women's Imaging Division. About UF Health: UF Health is the Southeast’s premier academic health center and an integral part of the University of Florida. Our mission is to promote health through outstanding and high-quality patient care, innovative and rigorous education in the health professions and biomedical sciences, and research across the spectrum of basic, translational and clinical investigation. UF Health encompasses the Gainesville-based University of Florida colleges of Dentistry, Medicine, Nursing, Pharmacy, Public Health and Health Professions, and Veterinary Medicine; the UF Health Shands family of hospitals in Gainesville; UF Health Jacksonville medical center; UF Health North; an academic campus in Jacksonville that is home to the UF College of Medicine – Jacksonville and includes degree programs offered by the colleges of Nursing and Pharmacy; UF Health St. Johns in St. Augustine; UF Health Neighborhood Hospital in Ocala; and our campus in Central Florida, which includes UF Health Spanish Plaines Hospital and UF Health Leesburg Hospital. It also includes primary care and specialty practices throughout Central, North Central and northern Florida and Southeast Georgia. The UF Health network of hospitals and physician practices manages more than 3 million inpatient and outpatient visits each year, and serves patients from all 67 Florida counties, from across the nation and from dozens of countries around the world. About College of Medicine – Jacksonville (COM-J): The UF College of Medicine – Jacksonville is the largest of the three colleges at the Health Science Center Jacksonville. The college's 16 clinical science departments house more than 500 faculty members, 1,560 staff and 450 residents and fellows, as well as medical students from UF and around the country. We offer an incredible breadth of clinical training programs and proud to train many of best primary care providers and specialists throughout the region, the state and the country. Research, discovery and innovation are critical aspects of our clinical campus and we have some of the country’s leading researchers at our locations searching for and finding new treatments and clinical options. The UF College of Medicine – Jacksonville faculty, administrators, residents, fellows, students and staff work as a team in pursuit of our common mission — to heal, to comfort, to educate and to discover through quality health care, elimination of health disparities, medical education, innovation and research. To learn more about our college, leadership, mission, faculty resources, and the city of Jacksonville visit https://med.jax.ufl.edu/administrative-affairs/faculty-orientation-guide/. jobs.description: Summary: The College of Arts and Sciences is currently accepting applications for the position of Adjunct Faculty in Forensic Pathology. The forensic pathology course is designed to introduce students to the key aspects involved in determining the cause of a victim's fatality or injury. It covers the procedures necessary to identify the victim, as well as to assess the mechanism and manner of fatality, including natural causes, accidents, suicides, and homicides.
